subject: Feature request: Neal's overrelaxation for conjugate samplers

messages.author: 9c2c0c89a3d22b1b
messages.subject: Feature request: Neal's overrelaxation for conjugate samplers
parts:
Dear Nimble devs,

Neal describes a way to reduce the random walk of a Gibbs sampler by using overrelaxation, which seems very effective:

https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~radford/overk.abstract.html
https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-011-5014-9_8

His strategy, §5, seems especially suitable for samplers based on conjugacy, or for which the cumulative distribution function is available, as some of those used by Nimble. From what I've seen it seems that Nimble doesn't implement it at the moment. It seems that it would make Nimble even faster, so I'd like to propose it for future Nimble development.

I will try to create a Nimble sampler that implements it, and report on performance results – although this will take probably some time.

Cheers and happy new year to you all,
Luca

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Feature request: Neal's overrelaxation for conjugate samplers
parts:
hi Luca,

One of our main challenges in adding new samplers is less our developer time in coding the samplers and more knowing which samplers are worth investing in, and (in the common case that a sampler has tuning parameters) choosing good default values for those. 

So, yes, we'd be very happy to hear what you find in terms of performance of the overrelaxation strategy. In particular, it will be important to know if any improvement in mixing overcomes any additional computation time for doing the overrelaxation. 

And a final note that in many problems, the issue is dependence between parameters; it sounds like this approach is focused on one-at-a-time univariate sampling.

-chris
